flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by genetic engineering?
flashcard_questions.a: Modifying an organism's genome by introducing a gene from a different organism.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must the same restriction enzyme cut both the gene and the plasmid?
flashcard_questions.a: So the sticky ends are complementary and ligase can join them.

flashcard_questions.q: Which enzyme seals a gene into a plasmid during genetic engineering?
In genetic engineering, what is a vector?
flashcard_questions.a: A carrier that transfers a gene into a target cell, usually a plasmid or virus.

flashcard_questions.q: What has golden rice been engineered to produce?
flashcard_questions.a: Beta-carotene, to combat vitamin A deficiency.

flashcard_questions.q: What can happen if GM crops cross-pollinate with wild plants?
flashcard_questions.a: Herbicide-resistant superweeds form that are difficult to control.

flashcard_questions.q: Who proposed the three-domain system of classification?
Which molecule did Woese analyse to define the three domains?
Linnaean hierarchy from largest to smallest: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, ____, Family, ____, Species.
Which domain contains all organisms whose cells have a nucleus?
What is binomial nomenclature in classification?
flashcard_questions.a: Naming an organism with two Latin names: its genus then its species.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a community in ecology?
flashcard_questions.a: All the populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a population in ecology?
flashcard_questions.a: A group of organisms of the same species living in the same area.
One where species and environmental factors are balanced, so population sizes stay roughly constant.
